Wayfare is Meridian Studio's realtime departure-display program for Halcyon
Transit: platform displays for three pilot stations — Ashport Central, Ferry
Quay, Millbrook Bridge — fed by live vehicle-position data.

Scope agreed at the kickoff (2026-02-20) with Petra Lindqvist: sub-second
perceived freshness, outdoor readability, and a June ship date. The displays
speak MQTT (decision d-002) and went from per-display autonomy (d-003) to an
edge-gateway hub (d-008) after field maintenance pain. The palette is
green-and-amber for outdoor readability (d-009).

Team: Dev Okonkwo (firmware), Noor Haddad (renderer), June Park (design),
Bram Oyelaran (fleet), Katrin Ilic (QA), Theo Kanda (systems).
Shipped 2026-06-12; ship retro in m-008.

The Larkspur Archive is a digitized-collection platform for Bellweather
Books: scanning, OCR, searchable metadata, and an online viewer. The OCR
pipeline uses a remote OCR API over local OCR (decision d-004, informed by
the ocr-comparison notes); a later latency benchmark (s-006) showed archival
page scans running far below the assumed throughput, which sent Dev and
Silas back to preprocessing. The viewer is IIIF-based (decision d-011),
prototyped in s-010.

Team: Silas Brandt (data), June Park (interface), Dev Okonkwo (OCR pipeline),
Odessa Klein (user research). Rowan Ellery is the client sponsor; Quill &
Marrow advised the metadata descriptions. Mid-project review with Bellweather
is m-007.

As of mid-June the project is active: OCR continues at the corrected rate and
the IIIF viewer is in integration.

Retro after shipping Wayfare on 2026-06-12. What worked: the edge-gateway
reversal (d-008) collapsed the maintenance surface — flashing is now a
station visit, not a fleet archaeology dig; Odessa's platform contrast
testing made the green-and-amber palette readable in full sun; MQTT retained
messages recovered cleanly through network drops. What hurt: QoS 1 delivered
duplicate renders during reconnects — next time, dedupe on the display, not
in ops. Katrin's QA signoff checklist is adopted as the studio default for
client ships.

Context: Ashport Central's platform is sunlit most of the day; the first
palette washed out in daylight.

Options considered: the original blue-on-dark palette; green-and-amber after
Odessa's contrast testing at the platform (s-008) and the WCAG contrast
notes.

Decision: Wayfare's displays render in green-and-amber — green for live
departures, amber for alerts and delays — both testing well above the
contrast floor in daylight.

Consequences: renderer theming is a config swap; June owns the design tokens.

final_answer:
Based on the records, June Park is Meridian Studio's product designer and has made significant contributions across two major projects:

## Wayfare (realtime departure displays for Halcyon Transit) — **shipped June 2026**

- **Designed the Wayfare display interface** and **owns its design tokens** (green-and-amber palette for outdoor readability)【people/june-park.md†L1-L10】【projects/wayfare.md†L1-L19】
- Participated in the **Wayfare kickoff** (m-001) with Halcyon Transit where scope was agreed【meetings/m-001.md†L1-L13】
- **Collaborated with Odessa Klein on platform contrast testing** at Ashport Central's sunlit platform (session s-008), where the original blue-on-dark palette washed out and green/amber alternatives proved readable in daylight【sessions/s-008.md†L1-L9】【people/odessa-klein.md†L1-L9】
- The contrast testing directly informed **decision d-009** adopting the green-and-amber palette, with June owning the design tokens【decisions/d-009.md†L1-L15】
- Attended the **ship retro** (m-008) after Wayfare shipped on 2026-06-12, where the palette's readability in full sun was noted as a success【meetings/m-008.md†L1-L12】

## Larkspur Archive (digitized collections platform for Bellweather Books) — **active as of mid-June 2026**

- **Designed the Larkspur Archive's reading experience** (the online viewer interface)【people/june-park.md†L1-L10】【projects/larkspur-archive.md†L1-L20】
- **Prototyped the IIIF viewer with Dev Okonkwo** (session s-010), implementing deep zoom on full-page spreads, page order from manifests, and metadata rendering per Dublin Core house style【people/june-park.md†L1-L10】【sessions/s-010.md†L1-L8】
- The IIIF viewer prototype was demonstrated at the **mid-project review with Bellweather** (m-007) and welcomed by the client【meetings/m-007.md†L1-L12】
- Took on building a **wallboard-style collection status page** requested by the client at the mid-project review【meetings/m-007.md†L1-L12】

## Summary of Contributions
June Park's work spans **interface design**, **design system ownership** (tokens), **field-tested accessibility** (contrast testing in real conditions), **prototyping** (IIIF viewer), and **client-facing deliverables** (collection status page). She collaborates closely with user research (Odessa), firmware/engineering (Dev, Noor), and client stakeholders.
